text:
marco: sketching a lightweight flow for handling late telemetry reprocesses with a cost-first mode. dropping here for feedback before I open an RFC.

marco: goal: let tenants opt into cheaper replay lanes that accept higher preemption risk. provide clear console UX and billing traceability. keep default behavior unchanged.

tara: high level sounds good. what are the lanes? preemptible, shared, reserved?

marco: propose three: preemptible (lowest $/token, can be killed), burst-shared (best-effort, medium cost), reserved (SLA-backed). policies map urgency -> lane, but user can override.

lin: important: we need distinct quota counters. otherwise shared capacity will be gobbled by preemptible jobs.

marco: agree. plan: replay.quota.{preemptible,shared,reserved}. each tenant gets baseline for reserved, and a configurable soft limit for preemptible.console shows usage and burn-rate.

devon: for the console, can we show a per-job price delta if you switch from reserved to preemptible? that helps users decide.

peggy: +1. also show historical preemption rate for that tenant/region so users understand risk.

ops-bot: alert: region-us-west preemption spike 12% -> 28% in last 30m

marco: good point. the UI should show live-risk indicator and a suggestion to route to reserved if preemption > threshold.

lin: telemetry / billing: every replay event needs fields: replay.lane, replay.attempt_idx, replay.preempted (bool), replay.final_lane, replay.cost_cents. we can aggregate by tenant/day.

marco: yes, and include an escalation_reason string for when we auto-escalate to reserved. helps invoice reconciliation.

devon: what about behavior on preemption? do we auto-retry same lane, escalate, or fail?

marco: default policy: retry up to 2 times on same lane with backoff, then if still preempted, escalate to reserved if tenant has reserved quota; else fail and mark for manual retry. make this configurable per-tenant.

peggy: edgecase: double-billing if partial work already charged then escalated. billing team wants idempotent cost attribution: attribute costs to attempts and a final charge rule.

marco: plan: emit attempt-level cost events and a final settlement event with canonical_charge. billing will sum final settlement per-slice.

lin: scheduler impact: preemptible work should prefer nodes with lower GPU memory pressure and where KV-cache locality is ok. otherwise we risk high serialization cost.

marco: scheduler heuristic: prefer node with same shard or neighbor rack; degrade to cross-shard only if wait > 3m. use a locality_score in placement decisions.

devon: API change proposal: add optional fields to POST /v1/telemetry/reprocess: lane_hint, max_retries, escalation_policy. keep older clients working. sample: 

```
POST /v1/telemetry/reprocess
{
  "tenant":"fizzbuzz",
  "window":"2024-02-01/2024-02-02",
  "lane_hint":"preemptible",
  "max_retries":2,
  "escalation_policy":"auto_escalate_to_reserved"
}
```

marco: also return estimated_cost and risk_score in response so Console can show a quick preview.

peggy: simulation request: can we run a 14-day historic sim with varying preemption curves and produce: estimated cost savings, extra runtime, and fraction escalated? ops wants that before enabling.

marco: yes i can run sim. will use last 2 weeks of scheduler logs and replay metadata. aim to publish sim report by Tue.

lin: rollout plan: feature-flag gated, opt-in per-tenant for 2 weeks, gradual 10->30->100%. include kill-switch at region-level.

devon: telemetry dashboards: new panel under Replays: lane mix, preemptions by tenant, settlement discrepancies, avg attempts per slice, cost saved vs baseline.

marco: add to that a small audit table: replay_id, lane_history, final_settlement, escalation_reason, owner. will help debugging.

ops-bot: note: creating alert runbook for "replay-escalation-spike".

peggy: last ask: doc updates and a short Console tooltip that explains what "preemptible" means (may be paused/killed, best for dev or non-SLA dashboards).

marco: thanks all. i'll open the RFC + PR with schema and scheduler patch tomorrow. leaving a checklist: quota labels, api fields, telemetry tags, console previews, sim results, rollout flag, runbook.

devon: thanks — look forward to the RFC.
